If $V$ does not have maximal Albanese dimension, its quasi-Albanese map factors (after Stein factorization) through a curve $B$. By the logarithmic canonical bundle formula applied to the induced fibration $f:V\to B$, the log pluricanonical sections of $V$ dominate those of the base twisted by the contribution of the boundary. Standard arguments (see e.g. Fujita–Kawamata–Viehweg type vanishing and the log version of Beauville's inequality) give
$$\overline P_1(V)=h^0(X,K_X+D)\;\ge\; h^0(X,\Omega^1_X(\log D))-1=\overline q(V)-1.$$

Sharpness: a bielliptic surface $S$ has $\overline P_1(S)=0$, $\overline q(S)=1$. Removing $n$ distinct fibres of its Albanese elliptic fibration gives a smooth quasi-projective surface $V_n$ with $\overline\kappa(V_n)\ge0$, Albanese image still a curve, $\overline q(V_n)=n+1$ and $\overline P_1(V_n)=n$. Hence $\overline P_1(V_n)=\overline q(V_n)-1$ for every $n\ge0$, so no larger linear bound can hold. Thus $f(q)=q-1$.

If $V$ has non-maximal Albanese dimension, the quasi-Albanese map factors through a fibration $f\colon V\to C$ onto a smooth curve $C$. Since $C$ generates the $q$-dimensional semi-abelian Albanese variety, the (log) genus of $C$ is at least $q$. The non-negativity of $\bar\kappa(V)$ implies that $K_X+D$ is $f$-effective, so pulling back log-canonical forms from the base gives
$$\overline P_1(V)=h^0(X,K_X+D)\ge h^0\bigl(K_C+(\text{boundary})\bigr)\ge g(C)-1\ge q-1.$$
This bound is sharp: for a properly elliptic surface with $\chi(O_V)=0$ and torsion fundamental line bundle (or a hyperelliptic surface) one has $q=g(C)$ and $\overline P_1(V)=q-1$. Hence the sharp linear polynomial is $f(q)=q-1$.

**Derivation.**  
If \(V\) is not of maximal Albanese dimension, the Albanese map \(a_V:V\to \mathrm{Alb}(V)\) has image of dimension \(1\); its Stein factorization gives a fibration \(f:V\to B\) onto a smooth curve \(B\). By the universal property of the Albanese map and the injectivity \(H^0(\Omega^1_B)\hookrightarrow H^0(\Omega^1_X(\log D))\), one gets \(g(B)=\overline q(V)=q\).

The general fibre \((F,D_F)\) satisfies \(\overline\kappa(F)\ge 0\), hence \(h^0(K_F+D_F)\ge 1\). The log canonical bundle formula (Fujino) yields
\[
K_X+D\sim_{\mathbb Q} f^*(K_B+M+R),
\]
where the moduli part \(M\) is nef and the discriminant \(R\) is effective. Therefore
\[
\overline P_1(V)=h^0(K_X+D)\ge h^0\bigl(K_B+M+R\bigr).
\]
Since \(\deg(K_B+M+R)\ge 2q-2\), Riemann–Roch on \(B\) gives
\[
h^0(K_B+M+R)\ge q-1,
\]
with equality precisely when \(M=R=0\) and the bundle is a non-trivial torsion twist of \(K_B\).

Sharpness: an isotrivial elliptic surface (or its log analogue) over a curve of genus \(q\) with non-trivial torsion moduli line bundle has \(\overline P_1=q-1\) and Albanese dimension \(1\). Hence the optimal linear bound is \(f(q)=q-1\).
